basic_info.title: MuDreamer: Learning Predictive World Models without Reconstruction

method.notes: Directly modifies DreamerV3 by removing pixel-reconstruction losses entirely, instead training representations by predicting the environment's VALUE FUNCTION and previously-selected ACTIONS. States that removing reconstruction improves robustness to visual distractions (task-irrelevant input the decoder would otherwise be forced to model) and speeds up training, while identifying batch normalization as necessary to prevent a DIFFERENT training collapse once reconstruction is removed. This is the closest same-lineage (explicit DreamerV3 successor) confirmation that a powerful reconstruction decoder is itself a source of representation problems, directly supporting the 'extend z-only isolation from RoadScorer to the MDN GPS head too' idea raised as the next Stage-2 experiment.

gap_analysis.whats_missing: General RL benchmark paper (Atari/DMC-style), not GPS map matching. Confirms the reconstruction-free design pattern within the Dreamer lineage specifically, but never touches road graphs or GPS.
gap_analysis.novelty_reasoning: Same class as TD-MPC2/Think2Drive -- architectural inspiration, wrong domain; does not pre-empt the thesis's GPS map-matching application.

relevance.bmw_relevance: Not directly BMW-relevant; the single most directly applicable precedent for the recommended next Stage-2 experiment -- since MuDreamer is a DreamerV3 successor (same lineage as this project's RSSM) that resolves decoder-vs-latent competition by removing/de-weighting reconstruction, this supports extending Change 13's z-only isolation trick from the RoadScorer head to the MDN GPS decode head as well, rather than inventing a new mechanism.

uncertain: Whether MuDreamer's batch-normalization requirement (needed to prevent a new collapse mode once reconstruction is removed) would also apply to Stage-2's GRU+categorical-latent setup was not verified -- flagged as an implementation risk if this direction is pursued.
